title: Launch safety net orchestration and standard incident comms forms
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Define an actionable safety-net orchestration for the upcoming runtime-1.22 launch and deliver a set of standardized incident communication templates for internal and external stakeholders. Scope:
- Define blocker criteria and fast-decision checklist for launch hold/abort.
- Create rollback playbook that is executable by SRE + runtime teams in under 30 minutes.
- Produce three communication templates: internal alert, customer-facing outage message, post-mortem summary.
- Coordinate ownership and escalation matrix across Eng, SRE, Product, Design, and Support.
Acceptance criteria:
- Blocker checklist approved by Eng leads and PMs.
- Rollback runbook has been dry-run once with SREs and documented outcomes.
- Communication templates stored in Confluence + Drive and signed off by Legal for customer-facing copy.
- On-call rotations and contact roster verified, escalation tests completed (paging and Slack templates validated).
Out of scope: long-term GTM comms beyond the first 24-hour incident window (handled by marketing), model quality regression playbooks (owned by Applied ML).
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff completed with Eng, SRE, Console, Legal. Agreed to prefer a single-stage rollback for runtime artifacts unless partial fallback is possible.
2026-03-04 - Jordan Lee (SRE): Draft rollback playbook ready. Need to validate KV cache invalidation step—possible edge-case for long-lived sessions. Scheduled dry-run 2026-03-09.
2026-03-09 - Ravi Singh: Dry-run notes attached. Two timing issues found during traffic drain; adjusted drain window from 10m -> 6m with staggered worker termination. Updated runbook in Drive.
2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Legal): Reviewed customer-facing outage copy; suggested removing any forward-looking performance promises. Updated templates accordingly.

2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: SLO impact thresholds finalized. Trigger criteria for rollback: P50 latency > 2x baseline for 15+ min OR error rate > 5% for 5+ min OR persistent data-privacy event. Added to decision tree.
rollback_trigger_criteria: Latency: P50 > 2x baseline for 15 continuous minutes
Errors: 5xx error rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes
Throughput collapse: Request success throughput drops > 30% vs baseline for 10 minutes without recovery
Security/Privacy event: Any confirmed customer data leak or KMS compromise
Critical downstream degradation: Core database unavailability causing user-visible failures
rollback_steps_summary: 1) Declare rollback — PM + SRE + Eng lead; publish internal alert via #launch-ops and page on-call.
2) Traffic drain: initiate staggered worker drain (6-minute window) and stop new connections to affected pool.
3) Promote previous stable model/runtime image (tag: runtime-1.21-stable) to production using blue/green switch.
4) Invalidate KV prefixes for affected sessions where necessary; run cache warm-up on stable image.
5) Verify baseline metrics (latency, error rate, throughput) and confirm with SRE before marking rollback complete.
6) Customer comms: send pre-approved outage note, update status page, and schedule post-mortem within 48 hours.
communication_templates: Internal alert (short): '[LAUNCH-ALERT] Runtime-1.22 - Degradation observed - rolling rollback in progress. See Confluence PM-87420 for runbook. Pager owner: Jordan Lee.'
Internal incident (detailed): 'Timeline, impact, immediate mitigation, owner, next steps, actions required from teams — use template ID PM-87420-INT-01.'

Customer-facing outage (status page): 'We are currently experiencing degraded performance after a routine deployment. Our team is executing an immediate rollback. We expect restoration within 60 minutes. We will follow up with a detailed post-mortem.'

Customer follow-up (post-rollback): 'Service has been restored to stable state (runtime-1.21). We are investigating root cause and will publish a full post-mortem within 48 hours. For urgent concerns contact support@redwood.com.'
Post-mortem summary: 'Impact, timeline, root cause, corrective actions, preventative measures, owners, ETA for fixes — template ID PM-87420-PM-01.'
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Agreed to prefer single-stage full rollback over partial model fallbacks to minimize state divergence (decision by Eng leads).
2026-03-04: Decided to move to 6-minute staggered worker drain after dry-run timing issues (SRE recommendation).
2026-03-09: Legal sign-off required for any customer email; status page messages cleared by product + legal.
2026-03-10: Add privacy/security event as an automatic rollback trigger (Zara Ibrahim).
